note: Lean's translation law inserts the derivative field `V.deriv` at x0; the equality with the x0-derivative of the correlator comes separately from `Derivatives`, and the rotation law inserts `lie` for L_d(K).

snippet.text:
structure StressLaws (Y : ∀ d : ℕ, Axis → S.Field d →ₗ[ℂ] S.Field (d+1))
    (A : ∀ d : ℕ, Ortho.Skew →ₗ[ℝ] (S.Field d →ₗ[ℂ] S.Field d)) : Prop where
  translation {n : ℕ} {x} (hx : x ∈ conf (n+1)) (q : Fin n → S.Tag) {χ : E4 → ℝ} (w : Window x χ)
    (b : Axis) (d : ℕ) (B : S.Field d) : shellGrad T J χ b x q B =
      S.useAt T x (Fin.cons ⟨d+1,Y d b B⟩ q)
  rotation {n : ℕ} {x} (hx : x ∈ conf (n+1)) (q : Fin n → S.Tag) {χ : E4 → ℝ} (w : Window x χ)
    (g : Ortho.Skew) (d : ℕ) (B : S.Field d) : shellSpin T J χ g x q B =
      S.useAt T x (Fin.cons ⟨d,A d g B⟩ q)

proof_context.conclusion: With `Y = V.deriv` and `A = lie`, `shellGrad` equals the table with the derivative field inserted at x0 and `shellSpin` equals the table with the rotated field `A d g B` inserted.

structure Derivatives : Prop where
  kernels (d a) (B : S.Field d) {n : ℕ} {x : Points (n+1)} (hx : x ∈ conf (n+1)) (w : Fin n → S.Tag) :
    S.useAt T x (Fin.cons ⟨d+1,P.deriv d a B⟩ w) =
      gradient 0 a (fun y => S.useAt T y (Fin.cons ⟨d,B⟩ w)) x

proof_context.conclusion: `Derivatives` identifies the table with `P.deriv d a B` inserted at x0 with the gradient in x0 of the table with `B` inserted.
